nodes.name: Obtaining a List of Distributions From Adversarially Corrupted Data
nodes.statement: In this remark, we show that if one is given adversarially corrupted unlabeled samples, then one can satisfy the guarantees of the above list-decoding model. Suppose that customcalD^star is a Gaussian distribution customcalN(mu^star,Sigma^star). Consider a data source that is (1-gamma)-corrupted for some gammain (0,1]: with probability gamma, the source outputs a sample from customcalD^star, and, otherwise with probability 1-gamma, it outputs an arbitrary sample that may depend on the past samples and the knowledge of the learning algorithm. In crefsec:advCorruption, we show that one can efficiently convert an (1-gamma)-corrupted source for any gamma>0, into one satisfying the requirements of the List Decoding PIU Model with ell= poly(nfrac1gamma). Moreover, under mild assumptions, we also extend this to the case where customcalD^star is an exponential family distribution.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{rem:list}
  In this remark, we show that if one is given adversarially corrupted unlabeled samples, then one can satisfy the guarantees of the above list-decoding model. Suppose that $\customcal{D}^\star$ is a Gaussian distribution $\customcal{N}(\mu^\star,\Sigma^\star)$. Consider a data source that is $(1-\gamma)$-corrupted for some $\gamma\in (0,1]$: with probability $\gamma$, the source outputs a sample from $\customcal{D}^\star$, and, otherwise with probability $1-\gamma$, it outputs an arbitrary sample that may depend on the past samples and the knowledge of the learning algorithm. In \cref{sec:advCorruption}, we show that one can efficiently convert an $(1-\gamma)$-corrupted source for any $\gamma>0$, into one satisfying the requirements of the List Decoding PIU Model with $\ell= \mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{1}{\gamma})$. Moreover, under mild assumptions, we also extend this to the case where $\customcal{D}^\star$ is an exponential family distribution.

In crefsec:advCorruption, we show that one can efficiently convert an (1-gamma)-corrupted source for any gamma>0, into one satisfying the requirements of the List Decoding PIU Model with ell= poly(nfrac1gamma). nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:ptfs:polynomials}
        Given $k\geq 1$, let $\hypo{P}(k)$ be the collection of all polynomial threshold functions of degree-$k$.
        A polynomial threshold function (PTF) of degree $k$ is a function defined by a polynomial $p\colon \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ of maximum degree $k$ and a threshold $t \in \mathbb{R}$ in the following sense:
        $H({p,t})\coloneqq \mathds{1}\sinbrace{p(x)\geq t}$.

nodes.name: Extensions to More General Notions of Smoothness
nodes.statement: The techniques we use to bound the sample complexity and computational complexity of PIU learning extend beyond crefasmp:smoothness. They suffice for PIU learning under the following weakening of crefasmp:smoothness: there is a known rate function rcolon R_geq 0to R_geq 0 satisfying lim_mto 0^+ r(m)=0 such that the pair of distributions inparencustomcalD, customcalD^star satisfy \[ for any measurable set S\,, r(customcalD^star(S))leq customcalD(S)\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] This captures crefasmp:smoothness when r(m)=(sigma m)^q. This additional generality also allows our framework to extend to settings where we can only ensure klcustomcalD^starcustomcalD=O(1) (see crefsec:klBoundsSatisfyGeneralSmoothness for details). This is important as crefasmp:smoothness does not hold in this setting for any finite sigma or q. nodes.name: Polynomial Approximability
nodes.statement: Fix a concept hcolon R^d to inbrace0,1, distribution customcalD over R^d, numbers k,pgeq 1, and constant varepsilon>0. h(cdot) is said to be varepsilon-approximable by degree-k polynomials in L_p-norm with respect to customcalD if there exists a degree-k polynomial fcolon R^dtoR such that \[ inparenoperatornamewithlimitsE_xsim customcalDabsf(x)-h(x)^p^sfrac1p < varepsilon\,. \] (For sets, we simply replace h(x) with the indicator of the set, i.e., mathds1_H(x).) Moreover, a hypothesis class hypoH is said to be varepsilon-approximable by degree-k polynomials in L_p-norm with respect to a family of distributions hypoD if, for each hin hypoH and customcalDin hypoD, h is varepsilon-approximable by degree-k polynomials in L_p-norm with respect to customcalD.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:poly_approx}
                Fix a concept $h\colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \inbrace{0,1}$, distribution $\customcal{D}$ over $\mathbb{R}^d$, numbers $k,p\geq 1$, and constant $\varepsilon>0$.
                $h(\cdot)$ is said to be $\varepsilon$-approximable by degree-$k$ polynomials in $L_p$-norm with respect to $\customcal{D}$ if there exists a degree-$k$ polynomial $f\colon \mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ such that 
                \[
                    \inparen{\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{x\sim \customcal{D}}{\abs{f(x)-h(x)}^p}}^{\sfrac{1}{p}} < \varepsilon\,.  
                \]
                (For sets, we simply replace $h(x)$ with the indicator of the set, \textit{i.e.}{}, $\mathds{1}_H(x)$.)
                Moreover, a hypothesis class $\hypo{H}$ is said to be $\varepsilon$-approximable by degree-$k$ polynomials in $L_p$-norm with respect to a family of distributions $\hypo{D}$ if, for each $h\in \hypo{H}$ and $\customcal{D}\in \hypo{D}$, $h$ is  $\varepsilon$-approximable by degree-$k$ polynomials in $L_p$-norm with respect to $\customcal{D}$.

Moreover, a hypothesis class hypoH is said to be varepsilon-approximable by degree-k polynomials in L_p-norm with respect to a family of distributions hypoD if, for each hin hypoH and customcalDin hypoD, h is varepsilon-approximable by degree-k polynomials in L_p-norm with respect to customcalD.

            \citet{diakonikolas2024statistical} provide an SQ-lower bound for the -- seemingly -- unrelated task of Gaussian parameter estimation with samples truncated to an unknown set.

nodes.name: Testing Approximability
nodes.statement: crefthm:main requires the hypothesis class hypoH to be approximable by polynomials with respect to customcalD in L_1-norm. Many guarantees on polynomial approximability are known with respect to specific distribution families such as Gaussians. One way to test this guarantee is to test whether the provided samples indeed come from a Gaussian distribution. However, most existing distributional testers have prohibitively large running time -- exponential in d . Instead, if hypoH satisfies a slightly stronger property that it has sandwiching polynomials with respect to the underlying distribution, then one can use Theorem 3.2 of citetgollakota2023momentMatching that gives a tester that runs in poly(d^k,nfrac1varepsilon) time. In particular, the tester comes with the following guarantees. [itemsep=0pt] item (Completeness) It says Yes if samples are drawn from distribution customcalD; item (Soundness) If this tester says Yes on samples S, then with high probability, varepsilon-L_1-approximating polynomials exist with respect to the empirical distribution whcustomcalD over the samples S.footnote To be precise, their result actually shows the existence of L_1-sandwiching polynomials, which is sufficient for us since L_1-sandwiching (whose definition is not relevant here) is a stronger requirement than L_1-approximation. Now, we can run the algorithm in crefthm:main with respect to the empirical distribution whcustomcalD. To use crefthm:main, we need to verify that customcalD^star is smooth with respect to customcalD^star in the sense of crefasmp:smoothness. By standard VC theory for sufficiently large samples uniform convergence holds with respect to degree-k polynomials, yielding the following additive-relaxation version of crefasmp:smoothness: for any measurable set T, customcalD^star(T)leq (nfrac1sigma) \, inparensmashwhcustomcalD(T)+varepsilon^1/q. This weaker guarantee is sufficient to execute our proof as we only use assumption crefasmp:smoothness mboxfor sets T whose mass is bounded away from 0.

nodes.name: Necessity of Improper Learners for PIU Learning
nodes.statement: To illustrate that improper learners are necessary, consider the class of one-dimensional halfspaces (i.e., thresholds with a ``direction''). Define \[ h_leq 1 = \ x in R : x leq 1 \ qquadtextand h_geq -1 = \ x in R : x geq -1 \\,. \] Let the two ``true" unlabeled distributions be \[ customcalD^star_1 = Unif[-2,1] qquadtextand customcalD^star_-1 = Unif[-1,2]\,. \] We now consider two PIU learning instances defined by (a): unlabeled distribution customcalD^star_1 with optimal hypothesis h_leq 1 and (b): unlabeled distribution customcalD^star_-1 with optimal hypothesis h_geq -1. Note that both instances yield the same positive sample distribution, customcalP^star = Unif[-1,1]. Let the imperfect unlabeled distribution for both instances be customcalD = Unif[-2,2]; which satisfy crefasmp:smoothness with parameters (sigma,q)=(nfrac34,1) in both instances. Since any deterministic learner cannot distinguish between these two instances, if it is proper (i.e., its output is restricted to one-dimensional halfspaces), it must incur a constant error on at least one of the instances. The same holds with probability nfrac12 for randomized learners.

\label{rem:necessityOfImproper}
    To illustrate that improper learners are necessary, consider the class of one-dimensional halfspaces (\textit{i.e.}{}, thresholds with a ``direction''). Define
        \[
        h_{\leq 1} = \{ x \in \mathbb{R} : x \leq 1 \} \qquadtext{and} h_{\geq -1} = \{ x \in \mathbb{R} : x \geq -1 \}\,.
        \]
        Let the two ``true" unlabeled distributions be 
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star_1 = {\rm Unif}[-2,1] \qquadtext{and} \customcal{D}^\star_{-1} = {\rm Unif}[-1,2]\,.
        \]
        We now consider two PIU learning instances defined by (a): unlabeled distribution $\customcal{D}^\star_1$ with optimal hypothesis $h_{\leq 1}$ and (b): unlabeled distribution $\customcal{D}^\star_{-1}$ with optimal hypothesis $h_{\geq -1}$.
        Note that both instances yield the same positive sample distribution, $\customcal{P}^\star = {\rm Unif}[-1,1]$.
        Let the imperfect unlabeled distribution for both instances be $\customcal{D} = {\rm Unif}[-2,2]$; which satisfy \cref{asmp:smoothness} with parameters $(\sigma,q)=(\nfrac{3}{4},1)$ in both instances.
        Since any deterministic learner cannot distinguish between these two instances, if it is proper (\textit{i.e.}{}, its output is restricted to one-dimensional halfspaces), it must incur a constant error on at least one of the instances. The same holds with probability $\nfrac{1}{2}$ for randomized learners.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{thm:sampleComplexity}
nodes.statement: The algorithm is presented in crefalg:sampleComplexity. It solves Tcoloneqqnfrac1varepsilon carefully selected instances of Pessimistic-ERM to obtain hypotheses H_1,H_2,dots,H_T and outputs bigcap_i=1^T H_i. The instances of Pessimistic-ERM are constructed iteratively, where i-th problem removes all unlabeled samples not in H_1 cap H_2 capdots cap H_i-1. [htb!] captionIterative-Pessimistic-ERM (from crefthm:sampleComplexity) [1] ProcedureIterative-Pessimistic-ERMvarepsilon,delta,sigma,q,hypoH vspace2mm State Set n=wtObinpareninparennfrac1varepsilonsigma^2qcdot inparenVC(hypoH)+lognfrac1delta State Obtain n positive samples P and n (imperfect) unlabeled samples U vspace2mm State Set T=nfrac1varepsilon vspace2mm For1leq ileq T State Define the survival set S_i=H_1cap H_2capdots H_i-1 if i>1 and, otherwise, S_i=R^d State Compute the solution H_i of Pessimistic-ERM specified by tolerance rho=0, positive item[] phantom....~~~~~~~ samples P, unlabeled samples Ucap S_i, and hypothesis class hypoH EndFor vspace2mm State return Hcoloneqq H_1cap H_2capdotscap H_T. EndProcedure We divide the proof of correctness into two parts. paragraphStep A (Bounding the number of false negatives): Each of H_1,H_2,dots,H_T is feasible for the Pessimistic-ERM constraint with tolerance rho=0 and positive samples P with absP=n. We claim that this implies that that with probability 1-delta, for each 1leq ileq k, customcalD^starinparenH^starsetminus H_ileq Oinparenvarepsilon^2qleq O(varepsilon^2) (as qgeq 1). We proved this claim below and for now proceed with the proof. Since Hcoloneqq H_1cap H_2capdotscap H_T, an immediate consequence of the above is that with probability 1-delta, \[ customcalD^starinparenH^starsetminus H leq sum_i customcalD^starinparenH^starsetminus H_i leq Oinparenfracvarepsilon^2varepsilon = O(varepsilon)\,. \] Proof of Claim.~~ Next, we prove our earlier claim. Let SinhypoH be any solution of Pessimistic-ERM with rho=0. By feasibility, it satisfies nfracabsS cap PabsP=1 and, hence, nfracabs Psetminus SabsP=0. Due to the choice of the sample size n and crefthm:unifConvergence, with probability 1-inparennfracdelta2, for each Rin hypoHcup inbraceG^ccolon Gin hypoH,footnoteHere, we use the facts that rm VC(inbraceG^ccolon Gin hypoH)=rm VC(hypoH) and rm VC(hypoH_1cuphypoH_2)leq VC(hypoH_1)+rm VC(hypoH_2)+1 . \[ customcalP^star(R) leq fracabsRcap PabsP + sqrtfracabsRcap PabsPcdot varepsilon + varepsilon\,. \] In particular, applying this to R=S^c (note that S^cin\G^c: Gin hypoH\), and using nfracabs Pcap S^cabsP=nfracabs Psetminus SabsP=0, implies that \[ customcalP^star(S^c) leq varepsilon\,. \] Finally, since customcalD^star( R )leq customcalP^star( R ) for any R subseteq H^star, it follows that \[ customcalD^star(H^starsetminus S) leq customcalP^star(H^starsetminus S ) = customcalP^star(S^c) leq varepsilon\,. \] paragraphStep B (Bounding the number of false positives): Next, we bound the amount of false positives. We claim that \[ absUsetminus H_1 geq abs(Ucap H_1)setminus H_2 geq abs(Ucap H_1cap H_2)setminus H_3 geq dots geq abs (Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_T-1) setminus H_T \,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] To prove this, consider any 1leq ileq k-1 and toward a contradiction suppose that \[ abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1)setminus H_i < abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i)setminus H_i+1\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Hence, in particular, abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1)setminus H_i+1 ~geq~ abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i)setminus H_i+1 ~Stackreltextupeqrefform@>~ abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1)setminus H_i\,. This contradicts the fact H_i is the optimal solution of Pessimistic-ERM defined by tolerance rho=0, positive samples P, and unlabeled samples Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1. Therefore, due to the contradiction, our supposition in crefeq:onesided:algo:contradiction must be wrong and, hence, crefeq:oneSided:monotone is true. Next, we will use the above claim to conclude that abs (Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1) setminus H_T leq varepsilonabsU. Toward this, observe that the following collection of sets \[ inbrace(Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_j) setminus H_j+1 mid 1leq jleq T\,, \] is disjoint and, hence, sum_i abs(Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_i)leq absU. This, along with crefeq:oneSided:monotone implies that \[ abs (Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1) setminus H_T ~~leq~~ fracabsUT ~~~Stackrel(T=nfrac1varepsilon)=~~~ varepsilonabsU\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Now, we are ready to prove the claim. Consider the T-th instance of Pessimistic-ERM constructed in the above algorithm, i.e., the one defined by unlabeled samples Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1. Since H^starsupseteq P, H^star is feasible for this instance. Let SinhypoH be any solution of Pessimistic-ERM with rho=0. By feasibility, it satisfies nfracabsS cap PabsP=1 and, hence, nfracabs Psetminus SabsP=0. We claim that \[ absUsetminus H_1 geq abs(Ucap H_1)setminus H_2 geq abs(Ucap H_1cap H_2)setminus H_3 geq dots geq abs (Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_T-1) setminus H_T \,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] To prove this, consider any 1leq ileq k-1 and toward a contradiction suppose that \[ abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1)setminus H_i < abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i)setminus H_i+1\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Hence, in particular, abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1)setminus H_i+1 ~geq~ abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i)setminus H_i+1 ~Stackreltextupeqrefform@>~ abs(Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1)setminus H_i\,. This contradicts the fact H_i is the optimal solution of Pessimistic-ERM defined by tolerance rho=0, positive samples P, and unlabeled samples Ucap H_1cap dots cap H_i-1. Therefore, due to the contradiction, our supposition in crefeq:onesided:algo:contradiction must be wrong and, hence, crefeq:oneSided:monotone is true. Next, we will use the above claim to conclude that abs (Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1) setminus H_T leq varepsilonabsU. Toward this, observe that the following collection of sets \[ inbrace(Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_j) setminus H_j+1 mid 1leq jleq T\,, \] is disjoint and, hence, sum_i abs(Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_i)leq absU. This, along with crefeq:oneSided:monotone implies that \[ abs (Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1) setminus H_T ~~leq~~ fracabsUT ~~~Stackrel(T=nfrac1varepsilon)=~~~ varepsilonabsU\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Now, we are ready to prove the claim. Consider the T-th instance of Pessimistic-ERM constructed in the above algorithm, i.e., the one defined by unlabeled samples Ucap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1. Since H^starsupseteq P, H^star is feasible for this instance. But since H_T is the optimal solution of instance T, \[ absUcap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1 cap H^star geq absUcap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1 cap H_T\,. \] Taking complements implies \[ absUcap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1 setminus H^star leq absUcap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1 setminus H_T ~~Stackreltextupeqrefform@leq~~ varepsilon absU\,. \] Since Hsubseteq H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T, the above in particular implies that \[ absUcap H setminus H^star leq absUcap H_1cap H_2cap dots cap H_T-1 setminus H^star leq varepsilonabsU\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Now, second-order uniform convergence (crefthm:unifConvergence) with respect to U and the following hypothesis class \[ hypoH_cap T = inbraceG_1cap G_2cap dotscap G_TsetminusH^starcolon G_1,G_2,dots,G_T in hypoH\,, \] implies that \[ customcalD(Hsetminus H^star) leq varepsilon + wtOinparensqrt fracabsUcap Hsetminus H^starabsUcdot fracVCinparenhypoH_cap T+lognfrac1deltan + wtOinparenfracVCinparenhypoH_cap T+lognfrac1deltan\,. \] Substituting the value of n, using that rm VCinparenhypoH_cap T=rm VC(hypoH)cdot O(TlogT), and nfracabsUcap HsetminusH^starabsUleq varepsilon (from crefeq:oneSided:empiricalUB) implies that \[ customcalD(Hsetminus H^star) leq varepsilon + wtOinparensqrt varepsiloncdot fracVC(hypoH) T +lognfrac1deltan + wtOinparen fracVC(hypoH) T+lognfrac1deltan leq O(varepsilon) \,. \] Therefore, crefasmp:smoothness, implies \[ customcalD^star(Hsetminus H^star) leq O(nfrac1sigma)cdot varepsilon^1/q\,, \] completing the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:main:assumptions}
nodes.statement: Due to the guarantee of crefthm:constReg, each of H_1,H_2,dots,H_T is a degree-k PTF over d variables. Since S_i is an intersection of at most T=nfrac1gamma sets from H_1,H_2,dots,H_T, S_i belongs to the family of the intersections of (at most) nfrac1gamma degree-k PTFs over d-variables, which has a VC dimension at most wtO(d^k/gamma). \itparagraph{Case A (For-loop breaks at iteration $i$):}
            First, suppose that the if statement first broke at step $i$, then the check in Step~\ref{step:alg:main:massCheck} (along with uniform convergence; as discussed in \cref{lem:main:assumptions}) implies that $\customcal{D}(S_i)=\customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap\dots H_{i-1})\leq O(\gamma)$ and $H=H_1\cap H_2\cap\dots H_{i-1}$.
            Therefore, $\customcal{D}(H\setminus {H^\star})\leq \customcal{D}(H)\leq O(\gamma)$. 
            Applying \cref{asmp:smoothness} yields $\customcal{D}^\star(H \setminus {H^\star}) \leq \sigma^{-1}\cdot \gamma^{1/q}\leq \varepsilon$.
            Further, since all previous iterations $1,2,\dots,i-1$, the for-loop executed, \cref{eq:main:constRegGuarantee} holds and implies that 
            $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H_i)\leq (i-1)\gamma^2\leq \gamma\leq \varepsilon$ where we used that $i\leq T=\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$.
            Combining these bounds implies that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\triangle H)\leq 2\varepsilon\,,
            \]
            completing the proof of correctness in this case.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:main:rejectionSampling}
nodes.statement: The only computationally non-trivial step in crefalg:main is the call to boosted constraint regression and the construction of and sampling from distributions customcalD_i and customcalP^star_i via rejection sampling. Since the assumptions of crefthm:sampleComplexity hold (see creflem:main:assumptions), it promises that the call to boosted constraint regression is efficient and runs in time poly(d^k,nfrac1zeta,lognfrac1delta). Hence, it remains to bound the time of rejection sampling. For this, it suffices to show a lower bound on the mass of customcalD(S_i) and customcalP^star(S_i) for each i so that it is not too small, since the inverse of this quantity is the expected number of samples from customcalD and customcalP^star one would need to see a single sample in S_i. We already proved this in crefeq:main:massGuarantee. In particular, the bounds in crefeq:main:massGuarantee ensure that each call to the sampling oracle in crefalg:main, with probability 1-eta, runs in time O((nfrac1varepsilon)lognfrac1eta) (for any etain(0,1)). Selecting eta to be a suitably small multiple of delta and taking a union bound over poly(d^k,nfrac1zeta,lognfrac1delta) calls implies the claim with only a logarithmic increase in the running time.

nodes.statement: The proof of creflem:constReg:expectedValue follows the ideas in the analysis of L1-Regression, but needs to account for some technicalities: First, unlike L1-Regression which selects the best threshold in [0,1] (crefalg:l1reg), crefalg:constReg has to select a threshold bounded away from 1 to ensure that the output hypothesis will be feasible for Pessimistic-ERM (which is required to establish crefresult:constReg:feasibility and, in particular, to prove creflem:constReg:feasibility:unconditional). In the proof, we observe that this only changes the expected value by a small amount. Second, the analysis of L1-Regression relies on the polynomial p_ensuremathOPT (which approximates H_ensuremathOPT) being feasible for the corresponding optimization problem. For L1-Regression, this always holds since the optimization problem solved by L1-Regression is unconstrained (crefalg:l1reg). For crefalg:constReg this is not always the case. But, we show that p_ensuremathOPT is feasible with high probability, and carry out our proof conditioned on this event. This conditioning does not skew the expectations significantly as the involved random variables are suitably bounded.

\label{thm:listDecoding}
            Consider the List Decoding PIU Model (\cref{def:list}) and $\varepsilon,\delta\in (0,\nfrac{1}{2})$.
            \begin{itemize}
                \item[$\triangleright$] (Sample Complexity)~~ There is an algorithm that, given $\varepsilon$ and 
                $\widetilde{O}\binparen{\binparen{\ell\cdot \sinparen{\nfrac{\ell}{(\varepsilon\sigma)}}^{2q} + {\varepsilon^{-3}}}\cdot \sinparen{\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})} + \log \nfrac{1}{\delta}}}$ independent samples from $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star)$, outputs a hypothesis $\wh{h}$, such that, with probability $1-\delta$,
                \[
                    \Pr_{\customcal{D}^\star}\binparen{\wh{h}(x) \neq h^\star(x)} \leq \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                \item[$\triangleright$] (Computational Complexity)~~ 
                    Suppose $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star) \geq \alpha$. 
                    Let $k \geq 1$ be such that $\hypo{H}$ is $\zeta$-approximable by degree-$k$ polynomials in the $L_1$-norm with respect to $\customcal{D}_{i^\star}$ for the index $i^\star$ in \cref{def:list} and $\zeta\leq O\sinparen{{\alpha^3\sigma}{}}^{2q}\cdot \sinparen{\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell}}^{1+4q}$.
                    There is a polynomial time algorithm that given $n=\mathrm{poly}(d^k, \nfrac{1}{\zeta}, \nfrac{\ell}{\varepsilon}, \log \nfrac{1}{\delta})$ samples from $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star)$ and $\customcal{D}_1,\customcal{D}_2,\dots,\customcal{D}_\ell$, outputs a hypothesis $\wh{h}$ such that, with probability $1-\delta$,
                    \[

                    \]

            \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: First, we prove the computational complexity result. The proof of the sample complexity result is analogous and is presented at the end. paragraphComputational Complexity. The algorithm in crefthm:main is not directly applicable in the List Decoding PIU Model because we do not know the index i^star of the distribution that is ``close'' to customcalD^star. However, the simple extension of the algorithm in crefthm:main described in crefalg:listDecoding works. Since each call to crefalg:main uses n=poly(d^k, nfrac1zeta, nfracellvarepsilon, log nfrac1delta) samples and runs in poly(n) time, the sample complexity and running time claimed in the theorem hold. It remains to prove the correctness of crefalg:listDecoding. Toward this, we claim that, with probability 1-delta, the hypothesis H^(1),H^(2),dots,H^(ell) satisfy the following properties. It remains to prove that Properties~, , and hold with probability 1-delta. Property~ follows immediately from crefthm:main since the distribution customcalD_i^star satisfies the conditions required by crefthm:main by definition of the list decoding model. To prove Properties~ and , let hypoP_cap 1/varepsilon(k) denote the hypothesis class of intersections of (nfrac1varepsilon) degree-k PTFs which has VC dimension wtOsinparennfracd^kvarepsilon; hence, in particular, O(nfracvarepsilonell)-uniform convergence holds with respect to the set of samples P constructed in crefalg:listDecoding and the class hypoP_cap 1/varepsilon(k). nodes.name: Proof of \cref{cor:truncation}
nodes.statement: This result follows by combining crefthm:main with the reduction in Corollary 6.13 in the arXiv version of . The reduction converts the estimation problem in crefcor:truncation to the following learning problem in poly(nfracd(varepsilonalpha)) time: given samples from a distribution customcalD=customcalE(theta_0) that is close to customcalD^star=customcalE(theta^star) in a sense stronger than that of crefasmp:smoothness with nfrac1sigma=q=C for C=polyinparennfracLambda(alphaetalambda), find a set S such that customcalD^star(Striangle S^star)leq varepsilon^O(C). This precisely fits into the framework of PIU learning with H^star=S^star and, moreover, since in the model of citetlee2024unknown, customcalD^star(S^star)geq alpha which ensures crefasmp:posFraction holds allowing us to apply crefthm:main directly.
nodes.raw_latex:
This result follows by combining \cref{thm:main} with the reduction in Corollary 6.13 in the arXiv version of \cite{lee2024unknown}.
        The reduction converts the estimation problem in \cref{cor:truncation} to the following learning problem in $\mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{d}{(\varepsilon\alpha)})$ time:
            given samples from a distribution $\customcal{D}=\customcal{E}(\theta_0)$ that is close to $\customcal{D}^\star=\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)$ in a sense stronger than that of \cref{asmp:smoothness} with $\nfrac{1}{\sigma}=q=C$ for $C=\mathrm{poly}\inparen{\nfrac{\Lambda}{(\alpha\eta\lambda)}}$, find a set $S$ such that $\customcal{D}^\star(S\triangle S^\star)\leq \varepsilon^{O(C)}$.
        This precisely fits into the framework of PIU learning with ${H^\star}=S^\star$ and, moreover, since in the model of \citet{lee2024unknown}, $\customcal{D}^\star(S^\star)\geq \alpha$ which ensures \cref{asmp:posFraction} holds allowing us to apply \cref{thm:main} directly.

nodes.statement: In this application, the samples are observed from the ``truncated'' distribution customcalQ(T) where T=R^d if there is no truncation and T=S^star if there is a truncation. Further, since customcalQ(S^star)leq 1-beta. To distinguish the two cases, it suffices to learn T up to O(beta) accuracy: this is because, for any set T' satisfying customcalQ(Ttriangle T') < nfracbeta2, if customcalQ(T') > 1-nfracbeta2, then it must be that customcalQ(T) > 1-beta which is only possible if T=R^d (since customcalQ(S^star)leq 1-beta). Now, the result follows from the sample and time complexity of learning in crefthm:main.

\label{new:thm:perm:robust}
        Suppose \cref{asmp:posFraction,asmp:smoothness} hold, allow ${H^\star}\not\in \hypo{H}$, and define $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\coloneqq \inf_{H\in \hypo{H}} \customcal{D}^\star(H\triangle {H^\star})$.
        Fix any parameters $\varepsilon,\delta, \gamma \in (0,\nfrac{1}{2})$ with $\varepsilon\geq \gamma > {\nfrac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}{\alpha}}$.  
        Consider the Pessimistic-ERM{} instance defined with respect to $n=\wt{O}\inparen{\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon}}\cdot \inparen{\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H})+\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}$  positive and unlabeled samples obtained from the two streams in the PIU learning model (\cref{prob:PUlearning}).
        Then, with probability $1-\delta$, any hypothesis $H\in \hypo{H}$ that satisfies:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho= \gamma $; and 
            \item $H$ is optimal (though not necessarily feasible) for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho= {5\varepsilon} $,
        \end{enumerate}

        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{H\triangle {H^\star}} \leq 
                \frac{144}{\sigma^2}\cdot \, \varepsilon^{1/q^2}
                \,.
        \]

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:perm:easy}
nodes.statement: Let TinhypoH be any solution of Pessimistic-ERM with rho=eta. By feasibility, it satisfies nfracabs T cap PabsPgeq 1- eta and, hence, nfracabs Psetminus TabsPleq eta. Due to the choice of the sample size n and crefthm:unifConvergence, with probability 1-inparennfracdelta2, for each Rin hypoHcup inbraceG^ccolon Gin hypoH,footnoteHere, we use the facts that rm VC(inbraceG^ccolon Gin hypoH)=rm VC(hypoH) and rm VC(hypoH_1cuphypoH_2)leq VC(hypoH_1)+rm VC(hypoH_2)+1 . \[ customcalP^star(R) leq fracabsRcap PabsP + sqrtfracabsRcap PabsPcdot varepsilon + varepsilon\,. \] In particular, applying this to R=T^c (note that T^cin\G^c: Gin hypoH\), and using nfracabs Pcap T^cabsP=nfracabs Psetminus TabsPleq eta, implies that \[ customcalP^star(T^c) leq eta+sqrtetavarepsilon+varepsilon\,. \] Finally, since customcalD^star( R )leq customcalP^star( R ) for any R subseteq H^star, it follows that \[ customcalD^star(H^starsetminus T ) leq customcalP^star(H^starsetminus T ) = customcalP^star(T^c) leq eta +sqrtetavarepsilon+varepsilon\,. \]
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $T\in\hypo{H}$ be any solution of Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=\eta$. By feasibility, it satisfies $\nfrac{\abs{ T \cap P}}{\abs{P}}\geq 1- \eta $ and, hence, $\nfrac{\abs{ P\setminus T}}{\abs{P}}\leq \eta$.
            Due to the choice of the sample size $n$ and \cref{thm:unifConvergence}, with probability $1-\inparen{\nfrac{\delta}{2}}$, for each $R\in \hypo{H}\cup \inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$,\footnote{Here, we use the facts that $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}=\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$ and $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H}_1\cup\hypo{H}_2)}\leq {\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H}_1)}+\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H}_2)}+1}$ \cite{mohri2018foundations}.}
            \[
                \customcal{P}^\star(R) 
                \leq 
                \frac{\abs{R\cap P}}{\abs{P}}
                +
                \sqrt{\frac{\abs{R\cap P}}{\abs{P}}\cdot \varepsilon}
                + \varepsilon\,.
            \]
            In particular, applying this to $R=T^c$ (note that $T^c\in\{G^c: G\in \hypo{H}\}$), and using $\nfrac{\abs{ P\cap T^c}}{\abs{P}}=\nfrac{\abs{ P\setminus T}}{\abs{P}}\leq \eta$, implies that 
            \[
                \customcal{P}^\star(T^c) \leq \eta+\sqrt{\eta\varepsilon}+\varepsilon\,.
            \]
            Finally, since $\customcal{D}^\star( R )\leq \customcal{P}^\star( R )$ for any $ R \subseteq {H^\star}$, it follows that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus  T )
                \leq \customcal{P}^\star({H^\star}\setminus  T )
                = \customcal{P}^\star(T^c)
                \leq  \eta +\sqrt{\eta\varepsilon}+\varepsilon\,.
            \]

                We now prove the feasibility of $H'$.

Noting again that sigmaleq sqrtsigmaleq 1 and that the square root term can be absorbed as nfrac1qleq nfrac(1+q)2q, we obtain \[ customcalD(Hsetminus T) leq frac7+sqrt7+1sigma\, (9varepsilon )^1/q leq frac11sigma \, (9varepsilon )^1/q \,. \] Substituting this into crefeq:sampleComplexity:UBterm1:ub completes the proof.

The lower bound on $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]$ follows from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}, the choice of the sample size $n$, and the fact that $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$ and $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$\footnote{To see this, fix any sets $A,B,C.$
                    Let \(\hypo{F}=\{G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). For any finite set of samples \(X\), define the labelings \(L_{\hypo{H}}=\{X\cap G: G\in \hypo{H}\}\) and \(L_{\hypo{F}}=\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). 
                    Note that $\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}=\{(X\cap G)\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in{\hypo{H}}\}=\{L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):L\in L_{\hypo{H}}\}$
                    The map \(g\colon L_{\hypo{H}}\to L_{\hypo{F}}\) given by \(g(L)=L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)\) is injective, so \(|L_{\hypo{F}}|\le |L_{\hypo{H}}|\).} and, hence,
                \[
                    \textrm{\rm VC}{\bbinparen{\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}\cup \inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}}}}
                    \leq O(\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})})
                    \,.
                \] 
                Define 
                \[
                    T = {H^\star} \cap H\cap H'\,.
                \]
                Since
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H) = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                    \qquadtext{and}
                    \customcal{D}(H') = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(
                    H'\setminus T)\,,
                \]
                we have
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H)-\customcal{D}(H')
                    = 
                    \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)-\customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                    \leq \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)\,.
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm1:ub}
                \]
                We now bound $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$ in two steps.

                \paragraph{Step 1 (Upper bound on $\nfrac{\abs{U\setminus T}}{\abs{U}}$).}
                    Notice that 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        = \customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \end{align*}
                    \cref{eq:perm:closeToInf} and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}},~\zeta\leq \varepsilon$ imply that $\customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})\leq 2\varepsilon$.
                    Therefore, 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \]
                    Further, since ${H^\star}\setminus T \subseteq \inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H'} \cup \inparen{{H^\star}\setminus H}$,
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star} \setminus T)\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')+ \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                    \]
                    Therefore, 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon 
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm3:step1}
                    \end{align*}
                    We have the following upper bounds on the last two terms:
                    \begin{enumerate}
                        \item Since $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, conditioned on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$, \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterms23}, implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,\sinparen{3\varepsilon}^{1/q}$.
                        (Here, we use the fact that $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ by construction.)
                        \item Conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ (which implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$), $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.
                        Hence, \cref{lem:perm:easy} implies that $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq 5\varepsilon + \sqrt{5}\cdot \varepsilon+\varepsilon\leq 9\varepsilon $.
                        Finally, \cref{asmp:smoothness} implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}$.
                    \end{enumerate}
                    Condition only event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$.
                    Substituting the above two bounds into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm3:step1}, implies that 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T) \leq 2\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(3\varepsilon)^{1/q} + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{}{\leq}~~~ 2\varepsilon + \frac{2}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{q\geq 1}{\leq}~~~
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over the unlabeled samples and hypotheses class $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\cdot \varepsilon}
                        +
                        \varepsilon 
                        =
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Since $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$ (as $q\geq 1$), $9\varepsilon \leq 1$ (which can be ensured by rescaling $\varepsilon$ by a constant factor), and $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}$, it follows that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3+\sqrt{3}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        \leq  \frac{6}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:sampleComplexity:boundSamples}
                    \]
                \paragraph{Step 2 (Upper bound on $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$).}
                    \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:optimalityOfH} and the fact that for any set $S$, $\nfrac{\abs{(S\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}=\nfrac{\abs{S\cap (U\setminus T)}}{\abs{U}}$ implies that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Hence, \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:boundSamples} implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq  \frac{7}{\sigma}(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over $U$ and the hypothesis $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                        \leq 
                            \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            + \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q} \cdot \varepsilon}
                            + \varepsilon
                            = 
                                \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                                +
                                \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                                +\varepsilon \,.
                    \end{align*}
                    Noting again that $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}\leq 1$ and that the square root term can be absorbed as $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$, we obtain
                    \[
                            \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                            \leq \frac{7+\sqrt{7}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \,.
                    \]
                    Substituting this into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm1:ub} completes the proof.

nodes.raw_latex:
Consider any $k\geq 1$.
        We reduce the problem of realizable $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$} from (labeled) samples $(x,y)$ where $x\sim \customcal{D}^\star$ to $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning {$\hypo{H}$} from \textit{only} positive examples under the assumptions in the theorem.
        
        This reduction will work when the optimal hypothesis ${H^\star}$ has sufficient mass in given PAC learning instance, in particular, $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$.
        The desired result can be deduced from this reduction due to the following sample complexity lower bound for learning intersections of $k$ halfspaces by taking the limit $k\to\infty$.
        \begin{theorem}[\protect{\cite[Theorem 5.3]{neuralNetwork2009bartlett}}]
                \label{thm:PAClearningLowerbound}
                The sample complexity of $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$} under the assumption that $\customcal{D}({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$ is $S_{\varepsilon,\delta}(k)\coloneqq \wt{\Omega}\inparen{(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})(\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H}_{\cap k})+\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})}$ for $\varepsilon<\nfrac{1}{8}$ and $\delta < \nfrac{1}{100}$.
                {In particular, if $\lim_{k\to \infty} \textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H}_{\cap k})=\infty$, then $\lim_{k\to \infty} S_{\varepsilon,\delta}(k)=\infty$.}
        \end{theorem}
        \begin{proof}[Proof sketch of \cref{thm:PAClearningLowerbound}]
                The proof follows by verifying that the hard instance created in Theorem 5.3 of \cite{neuralNetwork2009bartlett} satisfies $\customcal{D}({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$ and that the VC-dimension of {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$ goes to $\infty$ with $k$ by definition}. 
            \end{proof}
        

        \noindent In the remainder of the proof, we describe the reduction and prove its correctness.

        \paragraph{Reduction.}
        Fix an instance of PAC-learning {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$}, covariate distribution $\customcal{D}^\star$, and the optimal set ${H^\star}$ satisfying $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$.
        The reduction is as follows.
        \begin{mdframed}
            \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=-1pt]
                \item[]  \hspace{-6mm} \textbf{Input:} 
                    An accuracy parameter $\varepsilon>0$, a confidence parameter $\delta>0$, and
                    $n$ labeled samples $\inbrace{\inparen{x_i,y_i}\colon 1\leq i\leq n}$ where $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ are i.i.d.{} from $\customcal{D}$ and $y_i=\mathds{1}\sinbrace{x_i\in {H^\star}}$
                \item[]  \hspace{-6mm}  \textbf{Oracle Access:}
                    Query access to a PAC learner $\customcal{L}$ that learns from only positive samples 
                \vspace{2mm}
                \item Let the set of positive examples be $P=\inbrace{x_i \colon i\in \inbrace{1, 2, \dots,n},~~~ y_i=1}$.
                \item Return the hypothesis $\wh{H}$ obtained by querying the learner $\customcal{L}$ with $\inparen{\varepsilon,\delta,P}$.
            \end{enumerate}
        \end{mdframed} 
        Since $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$, we get that with high probability $\abs{P}\geq \Omega(n)$ and, hence, we only lose a constant factor of samples in the reduction.
        
        
        \paragraph{Soundness and Correctness.}
        To prove the correctness of the reduction, suppose $\wh{H}$ satisfies the requirement of PAC learning from positive examples:
            with probability $1-\delta$, 
            for each distribution $\customcal{D}'$, 
                satisfying $\customcal{D}'({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$ and
                $\customcal{D}'_{{H^\star}}=\customcal{P}$, it holds that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}'(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})\leq\varepsilon\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:lowerbound:PIUGuarantee}
            \]
        We will show that it implies $\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star}}\leq 2\varepsilon$, proving the result.
        Let the optimal hypothesis be ${H^\star}=H^\star_1\cap H^\star_2\cap \dots \cap H^\star_k$ where $H^\star_1,H^\star_2,\dots,H^\star_k \in \hypo{H}$.
        Without loss of generality, suppose that there is no set $S\subsetneq[k]$ with ${H^\star}\neq \bigcap_{i\in S} H^\star_i$.
        Otherwise, we can select the smallest such $S$, and continue with the remainder of the proof with $k=\abs{S}$ and the halfspaces $\inbrace{H^\star_i \colon i\in S}$.
        Define the following sets, which are useful in the analysis:
        \[
            T_1 = \mathbb{R}^2 \setminus H^\star_1\,,\quad 
            T_2 = H^\star_1 \setminus H^\star_2\,,\quad 
            T_3 = \sinparen{H^\star_1\cap H^\star_2} \setminus H^\star_3\,,\quad \dots\quad 
            T_k = {\bigcap_{i=1}^{k-1}H^\star_i} \setminus H^\star_k
            \,.
        \]
        We will only need the following properties of $T_1,T_2,\dots,T_k$: for distinct $1\leq i,j\leq k$
        \[
            T_i \neq \emptyset\,,\quad 
            T_i \cap T_j = \emptyset\,,\quad 
            T_i \cap {H^\star} = \emptyset\,,\quadtext{and}
            T_i \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2\setminus H^\star_i\,.
            \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:onesided:propertiesofT}
        \]
        The first condition follows from the assumption that there is no set $S\subsetneq [k]$ with ${H^\star}=\bigcap_{i\in S}H^\star_i$.
        The remaining conditions follow from construction.
        Consider the following sequence of distributions: for each $1\leq i\leq k,$
        \[
            \customcal{D}'_i = \frac{1}{2}
                        \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}} + \frac{1}{2}\customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}\,,
        \]
        where, for each set $S$ and distribution $\customcal{Q}$, $\customcal{Q}_S$ is the truncation of $\customcal{Q}$ to $S$.
        First, we verify that $\customcal{D}'_i$ satisfies the guarantees specified above.
        \begin{fact}
            For each $1\leq i\leq k$, 
            $\customcal{D}'({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$, and 
            $\customcal{D}'_{{H^\star}}=\customcal{P}$. 
        \end{fact}
        \begin{proof}
            Fix any $1\leq i\leq k$.
            It holds that, $\customcal{D}'({H^\star})=\sfrac{\customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}({H^\star})}{2}=\nfrac{1}{2}$.
            Further, by construction, $\customcal{D}'_{{H^\star}}=\customcal{P}$.






            
            
            
            
        \end{proof}
        Now, using \cref{eq:lowerbound:PIUGuarantee} for each of $\customcal{D}'_1,\dots,\customcal{D}'_k$ implies that: for each $1\leq i\leq k$,
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            + 
            \customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            \leq 2\varepsilon\,.
        \]
        Hence, 
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})\leq 2\varepsilon
            \qquadtext{and}
            \max_{1\leq i\leq k}\customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            \leq 2\varepsilon\,.
            \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:onesided:errorGuarantee}
        \]
        Now, we are ready to bound $\customcal{D}^\star(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})\leq O(\varepsilon)$:
        \begin{align*}
            \customcal{D}^\star(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            &= \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}) \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            + \sum_i \customcal{D}^\star(T_i) \customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
                \tag{since $T_1,T_2,\dots,T_k,{H^\star}$ are disjoint; \textup{\eqrefform@{\ref{eq:onesided:propertiesofT}}}}\\
            &\leq 2\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\varepsilon
            + 2\varepsilon \sum_i \customcal{D}^\star(T_i)
                \tag{by \textup{\eqrefform@{\ref{eq:onesided:errorGuarantee}}}}\\
            &= 2\varepsilon\,.
        \end{align*}

To prove the correctness of the reduction, suppose whH satisfies the requirement of PAC learning from positive examples: with probability 1-delta, for each distribution customcalD', satisfying customcalD'(H^star)geq nfrac12 and customcalD'_H^star=customcalP, it holds that \[ customcalD'(whHtriangle H^star)leqvarepsilon\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] We will show that it implies customcalD^starsinparenwhHtriangle H^starleq 2varepsilon, proving the result. Let the optimal hypothesis be H^star=H^star_1cap H^star_2cap dots cap H^star_k where H^star_1,H^star_2,dots,H^star_k in hypoH. Without loss of generality, suppose that there is no set Ssubsetneq[k] with H^starneq bigcap_iin S H^star_i. Otherwise, we can select the smallest such S, and continue with the remainder of the proof with k=absS and the halfspaces inbraceH^star_i colon iin S. First, we verify that customcalD'_i satisfies the guarantees specified above. For each 1leq ileq k, customcalD'(H^star)geq nfrac12, and customcalD'_H^star=customcalP. Fix any 1leq ileq k. It holds that, customcalD'(H^star)=sfraccustomcalD^star_H^star(H^star)2=nfrac12. Further, by construction, customcalD'_H^star=customcalP. nodes.statement: Fix any t>1, and define the set \[ T_t \;=\; Bigl\\, x in R^d : fraccustomcalQ(x)customcalP(x) \;>\; t Bigr\. \] On T_t, we have lninparensfraccustomcalQ(x)customcalP(x) > ln t. Hence, \[ klcustomcalQcustomcalP \;=\; int customcalQ(x)\,lnfraccustomcalQ(x)customcalP(x)\,d x \;ge\; int_T_t customcalQ(x)\,lnfraccustomcalQ(x)customcalP(x)\,d x \;>\; (ln t)\,Q(T_t)\,, \] which gives Q(T_t) le klcustomcalQcustomcalP/ln t. Next, split \[ Q(S) \;=\; Q(S cap T_t) \;+\; Q(S cap T_t^c)\,. \] On S cap T_t^c, we have nfraccustomcalQ(x)customcalP(x) le t, so \[ Q(S cap T_t^c) \;=\; int_S cap T_t^c customcalQ(x)\,d x \;le\; int_S cap T_t^c t\,customcalP(x)\,d x \;=\; t\,P(S cap T_t^c) \;le\; t\,P(S)\,. \] Therefore, \[ Q(S) \;le\; Q(S cap T_t) + Q(S cap T_t^c) \;le\; Q(T_t) + t\,P(S) \;le\; fracklcustomcalQcustomcalPln t + t\,P(S)\,. \] Since t>1 was arbitrary, taking the infimum over t>1 completes the proof.
nodes.raw_latex:
Fix any $t>1$, and define the set
        \[
        T_t \;=\; \Bigl\{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)} \;>\; t \Bigr\}.
        \]
        On $T_t$, we have $\ln\inparen{\sfrac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}} > \ln t$. Hence,
        \[
        \kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}} \;=\; \int \customcal{Q}(x)\,\ln{\frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}}\,{\rm d} x
        \;\ge\; \int_{T_t} \customcal{Q}(x)\,\ln{\frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}}\,{\rm d} x
        \;>\; (\ln t)\,Q(T_t)\,,
        \]
        which gives $Q(T_t) \le \kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}/\ln t$. Next, split
        \[
        Q(S) \;=\; Q(S \cap T_t) \;+\; Q(S \cap T_t^c)\,.
        \]
        On $S \cap T_t^c$, we have $\nfrac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)} \le t$, so
        \[
        Q(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;=\; \int_{S \cap T_t^c} \customcal{Q}(x)\,{\rm d} x
        \;\le\; \int_{S \cap T_t^c} t\,\customcal{P}(x)\,{\rm d} x
        \;=\; t\,P(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;\le\; t\,P(S)\,.
        \]
        Therefore,
        \[
        Q(S) \;\le\; Q(S \cap T_t) + Q(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;\le\; Q(T_t) + t\,P(S)
        \;\le\;
        \frac{\kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}}{\ln t} + t\,P(S)\,.
        \]
        Since $t>1$ was arbitrary, taking the infimum over $t>1$ completes the proof.

nodes.statement: The proof of this result uses techniques from citetcharikar2017learning. Fix beta= nfrac12. Let the (corrupted) samples be X=inbracex_1,x_2,dots,x_n and let x_1,dots,x_r be the set of uncorrupted samples from X. For each i, define f_icolon R^mto R^m to be the negative log-likelihood function, i.e., f_i(theta) coloneqq -loginparencustomcalE(x_i; theta). Let overlinefcolon R^m to R^m be the population log-likelihood, i.e., overlinef(theta)=operatornamewithlimitsE_zsim customcalE(theta^star)insquare-loginparenz;theta. Standard properties of the exponential density (see, e.g., citetdasgupta2008asymptotic) imply that: for all i and theta nabla f_i(theta) &= nabla A(theta) - t(x_i) ~~ quadtextand~~ nabla^2 f_i(theta) = nabla^2 A(theta)\,,\\ nabla overlinef(theta) &= nabla A(theta) - nabla A(theta^star) quadtextand~~ nabla^2 overlinef(theta) = nabla^2 A(theta)\,. Where Acolon R^m to R_>0 is the log-partition function of the exponential family and tcolon R^dto R^m is the sufficient statistic of the exponential family. crefasmp:exponentialFamily implies that f_i(theta) and overlinef(theta) are lambda-strongly convex and, hence, we can use . Before using though, we need to establish a spectral bound required by the theorem. Toward this, observe that for i drawn uniformly from [r] the expectation and variance of nabla f_i(theta) - nabla overlinef(theta) is bounded for any thetain Theta as operatornamewithlimitsE_isim Unif([r])insquarenabla f_i(theta) - nabla overlinef(theta) &= nabla A(theta^star) - operatornamewithlimitsE_zsim customcalE(theta^star)[t(z)] tagas x_1,dots,x_r are i.i.d. from customcalE(theta^star)\\ &= 0 tagas operatornamewithlimitsE_zsim customcalE(theta)[t(z)]=nabla A(theta) \,,\\ ensuremathoperatornamewithlimitsCov_isim Unif([r])insquarenabla f_i(theta) - nabla overlinef(theta) &= ensuremathoperatornamewithlimitsCov_isim Unif([r])insquare A(theta) - t(x_i) - nabla A(theta) + nabla A(theta^star) \\ &= ensuremathoperatornamewithlimitsCov_isim Unif([r])insquare - t(x_i) \\ &=ensuremathoperatornamewithlimitsCov_zsim customcalE(theta^star)insquaret(z)tagas operatornamewithlimitsE_zsim customcalE(theta)[t(z)]=nabla A(theta) \\ &preceq Lambda I\,. Now, we can establish a bound on min_1leq ileq knormtheta_i-theta^star_2 using a straightforward adaptation of the proof of and then, we show that this implies a bound on customcalR_w-divergence due to crefasmp:exponentialFamily. Using and above bounds on on the covariance and expectation of nabla f_i(theta) - nabla overlinef(theta), implies that with probability at least 1-e^Omega(beta^2gamma n), there exists a subset Gsubseteq [n] of (1-(nfracbeta2))gamma n ``good'' points that have a spectral bounds of S=O(nfracLambdasqrtbeta) and (by ) S_sfracbeta2=O(nfracLambdabeta). Now we are ready to use , which gives parameters theta_1,theta_2,dots,theta_k for kleq inparen(1-beta)gamma^-1 such that \[ min_1leq ileq knormtheta_i-theta^star_2^2 leq Oinparen inparenfracLambdabetalambda^2 cdot fracloginparennfrac2gammagamma addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \,. \] Next, we project theta_1,dots,theta_k to Theta(eta). With some abuse of notation, let the projections be theta_1,dots,theta_k. Since theta^starin Theta(eta), this only reduces the distance between theta_i and theta^star for all 1leq ileq k. Define \[ R = Oinparen fracLambdalambda cdot sqrt fracloginparennfrac2gammagamma \,. \] We claim that for any i, the customcalR_w divergence between customcalE(theta_i) and customcalE(theta^star) is bounded as desired (in both directions). To show this, we prove the following fact. For any theta_1,theta_2in Theta(eta) that satisfy that normtheta_1-theta_2_2^2leq R, it holds that \[ operatornamewithlimitsE_xsim customcalE(theta_2)insquare inparen frac customcalE(x; theta_1) customcalE(x; theta_2) ^w leq expinparen Lambda (wR)^2 \,. \] Where the w is as in the statement of crefthm:listDecoding:expFamily. [Proof of creffact:app] Observe that operatornamewithlimitsE_xsim customcalE(theta_2)insquare inparen frac customcalE(x; theta_1) customcalE(x; theta_2) ^w &= int e^w(theta_1-theta_2)^top t(x) + (w-1)A(theta_2)-wA(theta_1) customcalE(x; theta_2)d x\\ &= int e^ (w-1)A(theta_2)+ Ainparentheta_1+(w-1)(theta_1 - theta_2) - wA(theta_1) \,. Since theta_1 is in the eta-relative interior of Theta and theta_1-theta_2 lies in the affine subspace of Theta with normtheta_1-theta_2leq R, for the chosen w, theta_1+(w-1)(theta_1 - theta_2)in Theta. Since A is a Lambda-smooth function over Theta, \[ (w-1)A(theta_2)+ Ainparentheta_1+(w-1)(theta_1 - theta_2) - wA(theta_1) leq Lambda normtheta_1-theta_2_2^2 + Lambda(w-1)^2normtheta_1-theta_2_2^2\,. \] Using that normtheta_1-theta_2_2leq R, it follows that \[ operatornamewithlimitsE_xsim customcalE(theta_2)insquare inparen frac customcalE(x; theta_1) customcalE(x; theta_2) ^w leq expinparen Lambda (wR)^2 \,. \] Therefore, as for all i, theta_iin Theta(eta) and theta^starin Theta(eta), we can use the above fact with the bounds on the parameter distance (crefeq:application:listDecoding:paramDistance), to conclude that there exists an 1leq ileq k such that \[ renyiwcustomcalE(theta^star)customcalE(theta_i) ~~leq~~ fracLambda (wR)^2w-1 ~~leq~~ frac Lambda^4 gamma^3lambda^3 \,. \] This implies the desired result by observing that e^-Omega(gamma n)leq delta.
